solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cutting style leading to risk on short fashion

indicators.note: short means the word for fashion loses its final letter

parts.note: a trend is a fashion
something that leads to risk is chancy, i.e. risky

explanation.surface: A sharp design trend that flirts with danger in the fashion world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' reads as a fashion term for a sharp cut, but it is the incisive tone of a critic; 'short' clips the last letter of the fashion word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchancy is incisiveness, a sharp or biting manner of expression, i.e. a cutting style.

clue.text: Son's shunning fast food

indicators.note: shunning means the son's letter is kept out of the word for fast

parts.note: fast as in firmly fixed, stuck
S is the abbreviation for son; the 's stands for 'is', joining to the indicator

explanation.surface: A boy turns his nose up at fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: TUCK is British school slang for food, especially snacks and sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schoolboy slang, tuck is snacks and sweets, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Studying prolix rambles in English

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the abbreviation for English
rambles suggests the letters of prolix wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Reading a wordy text that rambles on in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambles' gives XPLORI from the letters of 'prolix'; 'in' splits the English abbreviation round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exploring a subject is to be investigating or examining it closely.

clue.text: Variable shade in ravines upset lean seabird

parts.note: a chine is a deep narrow ravine, a word used in southern England

indicators.note: upset tips the letters of lean into a new order

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird, thrown off balance, glimpsed in shifting light among ravines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LEAN into ELAN. A chine is a steep ravine, especially on the Isle of Wight and in Dorset.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese lantern is a collapsible paper lampshade that can be stretched or folded, so its shape varies.

clue.text: Authorise application to ramble

parts.note: an app is short for application software
to rove is to ramble or wander

explanation.surface: Signing off a request to go walking.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve something is to sanction or give official permission for it.

clue.text: Drape with the end cut short?

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off the idiom for the end

parts.note: 'it's curtains' is an idiom meaning it's the end

explanation.surface: A curtain hemmed too short at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the final S from CURTAINS, the idiom for the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a hanging length of fabric over a window, the American word for a curtain.

clue.text: Covers pimple over

indicators.note: over signals the word for pimple is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a spot is a pimple

explanation.surface: Concealer used to cover a pimple.
explanation.definitionFit: Tops are lids or caps, things that cover containers.

clue.text: Start working group

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Kicking off a working party.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning.

clue.text: Wanting Momentum to put party type before people

indicators.note: before puts the party type ahead of the people in the answer

parts.note: a stag (party) is a type of party for a groom before his wedding
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Momentum, a political group, is accused of putting party before people.
explanation.walkthrough: Momentum, capitalised, is a left-wing group in the UK Labour Party, which makes 'party' look political. A stag party is a British pre-wedding night out for the groom.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of lacking movement or growth, i.e. having no impetus.

clue.text: Certain marriage involves search leading to fit

indicators.note: leading to places the combined part ahead of the word for fit
involves means the marriage word wraps round the search word

parts.note: a union is a marriage
a quest is a search
able, as in fit or capable

explanation.surface: Wedding plans are said to be a sure route to good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' and 'leading to' are the placing signals; 'fit' means capable, not healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond any doubt is sure, so certain.

clue.text: About a month to dispose of large island

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: to dispose of means the abbreviation for large is thrown out of the month

parts.note: April is a month

explanation.surface: Roughly a month spent getting rid of a big island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dispose of' removes L from APRIL, leaving APRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian isle in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Dictator's supporter working to infiltrate crooked parties

indicators.note: to infiltrate means the working word gets inside the rearranged parties
crooked suggests the letters of parties are bent out of order

parts.note: on means working, as a machine

explanation.surface: A dictator's loyalist works undercover among corrupt political parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' gives PERISTA from the letters of 'parties', which 'to infiltrate' then splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peronista backed Juan Perón, the authoritarian Argentine leader.

clue.text: Left discussion meetings actor ruined

parts.note: gone means left or departed
fora is a plural of forum, a meeting for discussion
Richard Burton was a Welsh actor

explanation.surface: A troubled actor walked out on a series of talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the definition but it gives GONE; the definition is 'ruined' at the end. Going for a Burton is British slang for being destroyed or lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, RAF slang from the war, means to be wrecked, lost or killed.

clue.text: Under cover, with leg next to a particular duvet where length is key

indicators.note: next to places the leg word beside the rest of the parts

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket
the is the definite article, pointing to a particular one

indicators.note: where opens the instruction that one letter of the duvet word gives way to another
where length is key says the length letter is swapped for a key letter

parts.note: a quilt is a duvet
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Snuggled secretly under a duvet whose length matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side is also called the on side. 'where length is key' swaps L in QUILT for E, giving QUIET.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the quiet means doing it secretly, under cover.

clue.text: Innocence I found in part of church, note

indicators.note: found in means the I sits inside the church part

parts.note: the nave is the central part of a church
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Innocence discovered in the nave, with a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is a lack of worldly experience, so it is innocence.

clue.text: Just beginning new climb

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A climber starting out on a fresh ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something emerging or coming into existence.

clue.text: Clear near to meanders in river

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters within the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: meanders suggests the letters of near to wind about like a river

explanation.surface: A clearing close to where the river meanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meanders' gives ONERAT from 'near to', and 'in' sets it within the river. The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to clear them of blame.

clue.text: Tree on corner with rot

indicators.note: on means the tree comes after the other parts

parts.note: to corner, as in a market, is to hog it
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree on a street corner that has rotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corner' reads like a noun but works as a verb: to monopolise, hog.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash means nonsense, which is what rot means in British slang.

clue.text: Runner is more able to survive having run for the day

indicators.note: having ... for says one letter is put in place of another in the word
for, as in run for the day, means one letter replaces another

parts.note: hardier means tougher, more able to survive
D is the abbreviation for day
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner is tougher, able to survive a run for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: R replaces D in HARDIER. A harrier is a cross-country runner, as in many British running club names.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrier is a cross-country athlete, named after the hound used to hunt hares.

clue.text: Youngster absorbing one round number — who benefits?

indicators.note: absorbing means the young animal takes the one inside

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a youngster
I is the Roman numeral for one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A child taking in one round number and asking who gains.
explanation.definitionFit: Cui bono is Latin for 'to whose benefit', asked to find out who gains from a crime.

clue.text: Boasted about knight made king?

indicators.note: about means the boasting word wraps round the knight

parts.note: crowed means boasted
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight boasted about being made king.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that crowned is one example of being made king, the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is crowned at a coronation, made king by the ceremony.

clue.text: Accommodate striker, offering quick meal

parts.note: to quarter troops is to give them lodging
a pounder is something that strikes, pounds

explanation.surface: Housing a footballer and giving him a fast snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' wants to be a footballer, but here it is anything that pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter pounder is a big burger, a fast food meal.

clue.text: Regularly seen in sauna, vainly is one brawny men hit on

indicators.note: regularly seen in means every other letter of the two words is picked out

explanation.surface: A muscleman, frequently in the sauna, admires his own body.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every second letter of SAUNA VAINLY gives A, N, V, I, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith, a strong man, hammers metal on the iron block.

clue.text: Soldiers don't initially get better

parts.note: men means soldiers, the ranks

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of don't

explanation.surface: Soldiers fail to recover at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend is to heal or recover after illness or injury.

clue.text: Change of word order in reading

parts.note: a reading is a version or interpretation

explanation.surface: A grammar note on how a reading rearranges its words.
explanation.definitionFit: Inversion is the reversal of normal word sequence, as when verb comes before subject.

clue.text: Check fire's about right

indicators.note: about means the fire word wraps round the letter for right

parts.note: to fire pottery is to bake it in a kiln; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Making sure the fire is just right.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake is something that holds back or slows, a check.

clue.text: Yarn used in ornamental embroidery

indicators.note: used in means the answer is found inside the run of letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Yarn used in decorative needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' tempts as thread, which fits the embroidery, but it means a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long story, often far-fetched.

clue.text: Top after game advanced position

indicators.note: after puts the top word behind the game word

parts.note: bridge is a card game
the head is the top

explanation.surface: Coming out on top after a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a forward stronghold taken in enemy territory.
